audit_items.proof_trace: The only validation on `discord_role_id` in `teamSchema` is `z.string().min(1)` — a structural non-empty check with no allowlist membership test. No code anywhere in the actions layer cross-references the supplied `discord_role_id` against `generation_roles` or any bot-confirmed managed role set before writing to the database. Proof fails because all code paths that persist or mutate a team's `discord_role_id` (`createTeam`, `updateTeam`) bypass the required semantic guard entirely.
audit_items.attack_scenario: An attacker who gains admin access (feasible via the documented Supabase RPC auth-bypass in this system) calls `updateTeam` with `discord_role_id` set to a high-privilege Discord role ID (e.g., server admin or moderator). On the next `syncDiscordRoles` call for any team member, the Discord bot reads the DB and assigns that arbitrary role, escalating Discord privileges for all members of the targeted team.
